scripts.radio:
Good evening and welcome to Kenya on Record. Here is what matters for your pocket and your community this week.

Across our counties, traders are demanding straight answers on the four hundred modern markets promised by the national government. For thousands of vendors working beside roadside trenches in the rain, construction delays mean direct economic hardship—especially with Nairobi diesel pegged at two hundred and twenty-seven shillings and seventy-six cents a litre, keeping transportation and commodity costs painfully high.

At the same time, we have a vital compliance alert: do not fall for syndicates selling fake eTIMS invoices online. The taxman’s systems actively reconcile digital trails. Buying fake paperwork to lower your tax liability is outright fraud and will lead to prosecution and heavy penalties. Build your enterprise on legal ground.

On the national stage, citizens continue to debate whether broad-based political alliances serve the mwananchi or merely dilute vital parliamentary oversight.

Yet, our national heritage and green infrastructure remind us of what Kenya can achieve when public capital works: Lake Turkana Wind Power is steadily pumping three hundred and ten megawatts of clean energy into the grid, while Nairobi National Park continues to safeguard one hundred and seventeen square kilometres of unique wildlife habitat right on our doorstep.

Kwa ufupi: Wafanyabiashara wanataka masoko mia nne yaliyeahidiwa yakamilishwe haraka huku gharama ya dizeli ikibaki juu. Pia, tahadhari imetolewa dhidi ya ununuzi wa ankara ghushi za eTIMS mtandaoni—ni kosa la jinai. Kuwa makini, linda haki yako.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu. Here is your Kenya on Record briefing for the week.

First, small traders are speaking up loudly, demanding the fast completion of the four hundred modern markets promised across counties. Operating in open-air mud while Nairobi diesel sits high at Sh227.76 a litre eats away at every single shilling of profit.

Second, a crucial consumer and legal alert: steer clear of brokers peddling fake eTIMS invoices online. It is illegal, KRA’s audit trails catch up quickly, and the penalty is criminal prosecution alongside heavy back taxes. Protect your hustle.

Finally, as politicians push broad-based alliances, Kenyans are asking a valid accountability question: who checks the executive when the opposition sits in Cabinet?

Keep asking the hard questions, demand delivery on public projects, and stay legal. Have a focused week ahead.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Buying fake eTIMS invoices online is illegal. KRA tracks digital receipts, and buyers face severe fines and criminal prosecution. Keep it legitimate.
scripts.reels:
Four hundred modern markets were promised to Kenyan traders and mama mbogas. 

Today, thousands still sell in open dust and mud, while Nairobi diesel at over Sh227 a litre eats into every thin margin. 

Public funds were committed. Groundbreaking ceremonies happened. But until those sites have roofs, cold rooms, and running water, promises don't feed families. 

Kenya on Record is tracking these projects. Is the modern market in your constituency completed?
